summary: Susumu Sakurabe was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Otani University from around 1945 to 1950. He later served as a professor at Otani University from circa 1968 to 1991.

Susumu Shimazono studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1977). A scholar of religious studies and Japanology, he taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~1982–1987), University of Tokyo (~1987–2013), and Sophia University (~2013–2019).

Susumu Yamaguchi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied at Otani and Kyoto universities, and under Sylvain Lévi and Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He taught at Otani University, Kyoto University, and Kyoto Sangyo University.
Suwanda H. J. Sugunasiri, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Nalanda College. In 2001, he held positions attested at the University of Toronto and Nalanda College of Buddhist Studies.

Suzanne Karpelès was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 1917–1922. She later held a post at the French Information Bureau from circa 1945 to 1947.

Suzanne Newcombe is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Cambridge. She has held posts at Cambridge, LSE, Inform, King's College London, and Open University as senior lecturer in Religious Studies.
Sven Wittemann is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa (attested 2014).

Syed Ali Bilgrami was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Lucknow, IIT Roorkee, and University of London. He worked for the Government of Hyderabad (~1879–1901) and was Reader in Marathi at Cambridge (~1902–1911).

Syed Hasan Askari was a historian and Indologist who studied at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College (~1918–1920), and Patna University (~1920–1925). He later served as Director of the Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).
Syed Nawab Ali was a scholar in history and archaeology. In 1932, he is attested as Professor of Persian at Baroda College and Principal at Bahauddin College.
Sylvain Brocquet is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1980. He held a post at Aix-Marseille University around 2002.

Sylvain Lévi, an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held posts at the EPHE (~1886–1935), University of Paris (~1889–1894), and the Collège de France (1894–1935).
Sze-bong Tso is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982) under the supervision of Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.
Søren Sørensen was an Indology scholar who taught at Herlufsholm School (1876–1878) and held a post at the University of Copenhagen from around 1887 to 1902.
T. Chandrasekharan was an Indology scholar who studied as a pupil under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. In 1951, he was Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at The Madras Sanskrit College.

T. Griffith Foulk studied under Luis Oscar Gómez at the University of Michigan (~1978–1987). A scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, he taught at the University of Michigan (~1987–1995) and Sarah Lawrence College (~1995–2017).

T. R. Chintamani was an Indologist who studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras (attested 1938–1951) and was manager and correspondent for the Journal of Oriental Research, Madras (~1927–1943).

T. R. V. Murti studied at Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. A scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he held posts at Oxford (~1949–1950), Banaras Hindu University (~1953–1967), and McMaster University (attested 1982).
T. S. Devadoss is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who held posts at the University of Madras, attested in 1994 and as Professor in 2008.

T. S. Srinivasa Sastri was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where he was attested as professor between 1984 and 1992.
